assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
caveats: Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 89.2%, order-level 91.6%, technical 92.9%. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap.
341 duplicate attempts on 12 Oct were removed; each attempt is counted once.
Volume was about 39% above normal from 18 to 31 Oct; check the cause before comparing totals across this period.

facts.text: Attempt-level success rate for 1–31 October 2026 was 89.2%, from 384,193 successful attempts out of 430,580 total attempts.
The success rate depends on the denominator: 89.2% by attempt, 91.6% by order and 92.9% by the technical definition. The widest gap between definitions is 3.64pp.
On 12 Oct, 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts). The duplicates were removed and each attempt is counted once.
Attempt volume ran about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays from 18 Oct to 31 Oct (14 days).

response.headline: The payment success rate in October 2026 was 89.2%: 384,193 of 430,580 attempts succeeded, with each retry counted as a separate attempt.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the marketing or sales calendar for 18–31 Oct and compare merchant-level volumes in that period.
hypotheses.rationale: A volume spike of this size can come from a sale, but a data gap or backfill looks similar in the daily counts.
hypotheses.text: The 18–31 Oct volume spike is likely a real business event such as a sale rather than a data error.

recommendations.rationale: The three definitions differ by up to 3.64pp, so mixing them would give misleading comparisons.
recommendations.text: State which definition (attempt, order or technical) is being used whenever the October success rate is quoted or compared.
